description: Fixed before any source-grounding experiment inference. Public excerpts are new; artificial samples are not NASA quotations. Review checks are never sent to the model.

cases.text: The abundance of methane and carbon dioxide, and shortage of ammonia, support the hypothesis that there may be a water ocean underneath a hydrogen-rich atmosphere in K2-18 b. These initial Webb observations also provided a possible detection of a molecule called dimethyl sulfide (DMS).
cases.check: Preserve hypothesis/may/possible, abundance versus shortage, hydrogen-rich, and named molecules. Do not add a confirmed ocean, life or a biological cause.

cases.text: The inference of DMS is less robust and requires further validation.
cases.check: Preserve less robust and further validation; do not turn inference into confirmation or add life / instruments / test outcomes.

cases.text: While K2-18 b lies in the habitable zone, and is now known to harbor carbon-bearing molecules, this does not necessarily mean that the planet can support life.
cases.check: Keep habitable zone versus actual support for life distinct, not necessarily, and carbon-bearing molecules. No ocean, organisms or certainty added.

cases.text: Analysis indicates that this carbon likely originated in the subsurface ocean and was not delivered by meteorites or other external sources. Moreover, it was deposited on a geologically recent timescale.
cases.check: Keep likely, subsurface ocean, negated external origin and geologically recent deposition. Do not add life, exact age or chemical mechanism.

cases.text: Webb finds that on Europa’s surface, carbon dioxide is most abundant in a region called Tara Regio – a geologically young area of generally resurfaced terrain known as “chaos terrain.” The surface ice has been disrupted, and there likely has been an exchange of material between the subsurface ocean and the icy surface.
cases.check: Preserve most abundant, terrain description and likely exchange; no proven eruption, plate tectonics, ocean life or cause beyond source.

cases.text: Carbon dioxide isn’t stable on Europa’s surface. Therefore, the scientists say it’s likely that it was supplied on a geologically recent timescale – a conclusion bolstered by its concentration in a region of young terrain.
cases.check: Preserve instability, likely/recent and the stated evidential relationship; no numeric dating, source mechanism or confirmed origin.

cases.text: As a result, one important open question in astronomy is whether a rocky planet could maintain, or reestablish, an atmosphere in such a harsh environment.
cases.check: Keep open question and maintain versus reestablish. Do not assert an atmosphere, location or specific physical cause.

cases.text: If the water vapor is associated with the planet, that would indicate that it has an atmosphere despite its scorching temperature and close proximity to its star. Water vapor has been seen on gaseous exoplanets before, but to date no atmosphere has been definitely detected around a rocky exoplanet. However, the team cautions that the water vapor could be on the star itself – specifically, in cool starspots – and not from the planet at all.
cases.check: Preserve conditional atmosphere, no definite rocky detection in this historic source, and alternative starspot origin. Do not silently update old scientific claims or add oceans/life.

cases.text: It orbits a red dwarf star in just under 1.5 Earth days. It is expected to be tidally locked, with a permanent day side and a permanent night side.
cases.check: Preserve just under, 1.5 Earth days, expected and permanent day/night sides. Do not add confirmed lock or name/chemistry/temperature absent from selection.

cases.text: The length of the plume was not the only characteristic that intrigued researchers. The rate at which the water vapor is gushing out, about 79 gallons per second, is also particularly impressive. At this rate, you could fill an Olympic-sized swimming pool in just a couple of hours. In comparison, doing so with a garden hose on Earth would take more than 2 weeks.
cases.check: Keep about79 gallons/s, couple hours vs more than2 weeks and pool comparison. No extra ocean/ice/geyser cause or silently converted units.

cases.text: The Webb observations directly demonstrate how the moon’s water vapor plumes feed the torus. By analyzing the Webb data, astronomers have determined roughly 30 percent of the water stays within this torus, and the other 70 percent escapes to supply the rest of the Saturnian system of water.
cases.check: Preserve roughly30/70 and their destinations; torus is not ocean and source does not assert escape from the entire Saturnian system.

cases.text: Sandwiched between the moon’s icy outer crust and its rocky core is a global reservoir of salty water.
cases.check: Keep global salty reservoir between crust/core. Do not add confirmed habitability, temperature, thickness or a biological origin.

cases.text: The band travels at 240 miles per hour, twice the sustained wind speed of a Category 4 hurricane on Earth.
cases.check: Keep240 miles/h,twice,Category4. No ocean, landfall, rainfall or other location; comparison is source data, not a fact-correction task.

cases.text: The band travels at 240 miles per hour, twice the sustained wind speed of a Category 4 hurricane over the ocean on Earth.
cases.check: Keep ocean explicitly, as well as240 miles/h,twice,Category4. Do not delete ocean to avoid the known failure.

cases.text: The report compares this wind with a Category 3 hurricane but does not specify where that hurricane occurs.
cases.check: KeepCategory3 and unspecified location; do not complete a marine location, strength threshold or physical cause.

cases.text: The camera recorded clouds above a dry inland plateau. No measurements over water were reported.
cases.check: Preserve dry,inland,plateau,and no reported measurements over water. Do not add a mechanism, geographic name or observed sea weather.

cases.text: The signal may come from the star; it is not evidence that the planet has an ocean.
cases.check: Preserve may,stellar origin,and not evidence of ocean. Keep the explicit negated ocean claim rather than deleting the noun.

cases.text: The estimate is v = 2u, with u = 120 km/h. The report gives no physical cause for the ratio.
cases.check: Keep v = 2u, u = 120 km/h and no cause. Do not add derived speed, energy, wind mechanism or explanatory text.

cases.text: The sample contains carbon dioxide. Its origin has not been determined.
cases.check: Keep carbon dioxide and undetermined origin. No ocean,meteorites,life or a geological cause.

cases.text: The sample contains carbon dioxide from the subsurface ocean. No biological source has been established.
cases.check: Preserve subsurface ocean and no established biological source. Do not erase ocean or strengthen/negate the source claim.

cases.text: The newly discovered jet stream travels at about 320 miles per hour (515 kilometers per hour), twice the sustained winds of a Category 5 hurricane here on Earth. It is located around 25 miles (40 kilometers) above the clouds, in Jupiter’s lower stratosphere.
cases.check: Known old diagnostic, excluded from new-sample improvement count. Keep every number/unit/comparison; no ocean or added physical cause.
